content.title: Why companies are staying private rather than pursuing an IPO
content.description:
OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) has become the world's largest private company with a valuation of $500 billion, but the ChatGPT maker isn't expected to go public anytime soon, if at all. The artificial intelligence developer has also inked a deal with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) this week, giving it a 10% stake in the chipmaker.

Hamilton Lane (HLNE) Co-CEO Erik Hirsch explains that the shift away from an initial public offering (IPO) being the "hallmark of success" is an "evolution" of the market.

Also catch Yahoo Finance's full interview with OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar from September, where she weighs in on the likelihood of an IPO.
